date_note: The page gives only its publication day (23 November) for Next's statement; it states no earlier day for the incident.
title: Next says an external online service provider it uses suffered a cyber incident
geo_basis: country only; the article gives no city for the provider or the company
summary: Next told investors, as reported by PA, that a third-party online supplier suffered a cyber incident, leading to "unauthorised access to certain benign data relating to Next". Next says current evidence indicates no customer personal data has been compromised and the data cannot be used to facilitate fraud. Next also says, per Drapers, it is confident its own systems have not been compromised. It is working with the supplier, law enforcement and regulators.
plain: Next says a cyber incident hit an outside online supplier and some "benign" data relating to Next was accessed. Next says current evidence indicates no customer personal data was compromised.
exec: Next says a supplier incident allowed unauthorised access to some data relating to the retailer; Next calls it benign and says no customer personal data appears compromised.

sources.name: Drapers: Next reports third-party supplier cyber incident
PA News Agency via Enfield Independent

validation.note: Two publishers state the core fact: Calcalist (relaying Reuters) and PA News Agency (via Enfield Independent), the latter quoting Next's statement to investors. Next's own statement and the Reuters text were not read; the PA page shows no publication date; the Herald Series copy could not be loaded by the reader. Drapers (23 Nov) also quotes Next's statement, including that it is confident its own systems have not been compromised.

review.note: Re-read Drapers, Calcalist (Reuters) and PA copy: title, date, benign data, no customer data, own systems not compromised, supplier police regulators match; PA page has no date so published stays unset
